label: Kurultai succession settled
summary: Fires when a Kurultai succession has just been resolved and the new heir is in place.
details: The root is the new heir. Vanilla runs it only under the single-heir Kurultai succession law. The comments name saved scopes: `scope:was_kurultai` (whether the heir sat on the predecessor's Kurultai Council), `scope:kurultai_members`, `scope:obedient_kurultai` and `scope:disobedient_kurultai` (lists of characters). If the obedient list is not empty, vanilla gives every obedient member other than the heir an opinion of the heir for 5 years, and gives the heir a memory of a stable Kurultai succession.

label: Leave council
summary: Fires when a councillor leaves a ruler's council.
details: Vanilla uses `scope:councillor` for the character who left, and unblocks firing for them. A day later it fires an event that informs the liege that their councillor resigned. That event is sent by `scope:councillor` and is addressed to the root, so the root is most likely the ruler whose council it is, not the councillor. The game's documentation only says the root is a character.

label: Leave court
summary: Fires when a character leaves a court.
details: The root is the character who left; `scope:old_employer` is their former employer. It does not fire for death or similar departures. It fires just before `on_join_court` if both happen. Vanilla cleans up booner-target and salary-list variables on the old employer and their courtiers, clears a flag and a cooldown variable on the character, and fires an event that cancels the employment contract.

label: Left diarchy
summary: Fires when a liege has just left their diarchy (shared rule), after the diarchy is already gone.
details: The root is the liege who left. `scope:old_diarch` is the character who was the diarch. It can also fire on the liege's death or destruction, and the old diarch may no longer be a vassal, so check that the liege is valid and alive. Vanilla tells the liege's vassals, then cleans up the old diarch: conspiracy variables, the extravagance modifiers a vizier had, and co-ruler title variables. It schedules an intro event a day later if the old diarch is alive. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest is not shown.

label: Liberation siege done
summary: Fires when a liberation siege completes, meaning a siege that turns an occupied barony back into an unoccupied one.
details: The root is the liberator of the occupation. Saved scopes: `scope:barony` (the liberated barony), `scope:county` (its county), `scope:previous_controller` (the county's previous controller) and `scope:war` (the war that made the controller and the liberator hostile). There is also a list `liberated_baronies`: the game's comment describes it as the baronies the siege affected, including ones with no fort level, but its wording is unclear. Vanilla's definition is empty.

label: Liege changes government
summary: Fires for each direct vassal when their liege's government type changes.
details: The root is the vassal. Vanilla (marked EP3) checks whether the vassal's government has the administrative mechanic while the liege's no longer does. If so, it saves the liege and their primary title as `scope:gov_liege` and `scope:gov_liege_title`, and fires an event a day later to work out the outcome.

label: Marriage
summary: Fires when two characters get married.
details: The root is the major partner of the marriage and `scope:spouse` is the minor partner. It does not fire for historical marriages. Vanilla gives both a marriage memory, updates the consort opinions of the new spouse and all other spouses and concubines, and runs an effect about vassals disliking a lowborn marriage. It fires a follow-up event for the spouse when she is a woman carrying (or secretly having) the root's child. The vanilla text is cut off; it goes on with a check about blood brothers.

label: Mercenary company dismissed
summary: Fires when a mercenary company is dismissed, for example when its contract expires.
details: The root is the mercenary company; `scope:old_employer` is the character who had hired it. It may also happen on succession or on title and vassal changes. Vanilla removes the employer's nomad mercenary bonus modifiers. For a nomadic employer whose domicile has a mercenary-fired bonus, there is a chance (20, 40 or 60 percent by bonus level) that the employer gains a random knight of the company leader as a courtier.

label: Mercenary company hired
summary: Fires when a character hires a mercenary company.
details: The root is the mercenary company; `scope:employer` is the character who hired it. Vanilla gives a nomadic employer a modifier matching the hired-bonus level of their domicile. It also runs an effect that, going by its name, is a catalyst for the Christian church's clergy hiring mercenaries.

label: Merit level gained
summary: Fires when a character gains a merit level.
details: The game's own documentation names no root scope. Vanilla acts only if the government allows merit and the character is not the top liege: it shows a message, adds prestige, piety and influence in the amount set by the highest merit rank bonus (1 to 6) the character's domicile has, and fires an introduction event 2 to 10 days later for a human player. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest (it also deals with the elder and disciple relation) is not shown.

label: Merit level lost
summary: Fires when a character loses a merit level.
details: Vanilla shows a message if the government allows merit. It then ends the elder relation (the character as the disciple's elder) for every disciple whose merit level is the same or higher than the character's own.

label: Migration travel ended
summary: Fires the day after a ruler's migration travel ends.
details: The root is the migrating ruler. Saved scopes: `scope:actor` (the same ruler), `scope:recipient` (holder of the target title), `scope:target_title` (the higher title the migration aims at, any tier) and `scope:domain` (a county or duchy whose land becomes the ruler's new personal domain). Vanilla fires a migration event, applies the migration's title and vassal changes, sets an achievement variable for a human player under some conditions, and fires the `mpo_migration_finished` on_action.

label: Migration war ended
summary: Fires when a migration war ends.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use. Vanilla uses `scope:war`, `scope:target_title` and `scope:domain` here, but its text has no comment naming the root. When the war carries the `migration_victory` variable, vanilla applies the migration's title and vassal changes, fires `mpo_migration_finished`, and sends a message to other migrating rulers heading into the target (the message is named as an invalidated migration). It may also set an achievement variable for a human player.

label: Natural death second chance
summary: Fires when someone is about to die a natural death but is given a second chance by the `has_natural_death_second_chance` scripted rule.
details: The root is the character. Vanilla sets a 390-day flag and a flag that the delay has triggered, fires event `death_management.9998` at once and `death_management.9999` after 340 to 380 days.

label: Noble family title created
summary: Fires for a character when a new noble family title is created for them.
details: The root is the holder of the new title. Vanilla gives 100 each of gold, prestige, piety and influence to a character whose amount of that currency is 0 or less. A holder with a Japanese manor domicile under the Japanese feudal government has the domicile moved to their capital province if it is not already there.

label: Perks refunded
summary: Fires when a player refunds their perks.
details: The root is the player. Vanilla refunds all perks, adds stress (`refund_perks_stress_impact`), sets the flag `has_refunded_perks`, and runs effects that, going by their names, remove landless inspector modifiers and the lifestyle traits tied to perks.

label: Personal tenet gained
summary: Fires when a character successfully picks a new personal tenet.
details: The root is the character; `scope:tenet` is the tenet they just picked. If the faith's main rite prohibits that tenet, vanilla runs a secret-related effect (shown as a tooltip). It also runs many effects that, going by their names, hand out the traits tied to specific tenets (gardener, scarred, mystic, scholar and others), and updates tenet popularity.

label: Personal tenet dropped
summary: Fires when a character swaps out or removes a personal tenet.
details: The root is the character; `scope:tenet` is the tenet they dropped. Vanilla adds major stress to a human player unless a fulfillment parameter waives it, removes the divine liturgy officiant modifier if the character no longer has that tenet's flag, runs an effect that removes a forbidden-tenet secret that is no longer valid (going by its name), and updates tenet popularity.

label: Piety level gained
summary: Fires when a character gains a piety level.
details: The game's own documentation names no root scope. Vanilla acts only for characters whose government has the mandala flag. They get a level-gain message, and a notice at the maximum level (not repeated while a 5-day flag is set). Levels beyond the maximum create a memory. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest is not shown.

label: Piety level lost
summary: Fires when a character loses a piety level.
details: Vanilla shows a level-loss message unless the character has the variable `busy_in_mandala_succession`. It also lowers the `parent_piety_lvl` variable by 1 on each child who remembers the parent becoming very pious.

label: Player character changed
summary: Fires whenever the player switches from one character to another.
details: The root is the new player character and `scope:previous_player_character` the old one. Vanilla marks it as a hook for mods. It clears puppet status and puppet modifiers if the new character has a puppeteer, and runs an effect that, going by its name, offers the great schism stance to the new player.

label: First royal court
summary: Fires when a player gains a royal court for the first time.
details: The root is that player. Vanilla shows a toast message and fires court maintenance event `court_maintenance.0011` one day later (the delay avoids wrong text for the title).

label: Destiny character confirmed
summary: Fires when the player confirms the character they chose as their destiny.
details: The root is the chosen destiny character, who is already the current player. Saved scopes: `scope:destiny_type_flag`, `scope:previous_player_character`, `scope:previous_player_heir`. Vanilla gives a chosen character who is not a ruler a landless adventurer title, counts destiny choices in a global variable for an achievement, and sets achievement variables if the character is landed and holds an empire-tier title or higher.

label: Destiny choices set up
summary: Fires after a succession, to fill the lists of characters the player can pick as their destiny.
details: The root is the dead previous character; `scope:predecessor` is the same character and `scope:heir` the current player heir. Script is expected to fill `main_destiny_types` and `random_destiny_types` (lists of flags, possibly empty) and save a character under `scope:<flag of the destiny type>`. Vanilla adds three main types (interesting, favorite, hard difficulty) and collects living, capable AI dynasty members as candidates. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest is not shown.

label: Great holy war may be invalid
summary: Fires when a great holy war no longer has a valid target and nobody is left in the target kingdom to replace it.
details: The root is the great holy war. The target scopes still point to the last target. If script does not pick a new target, the war is invalidated. Vanilla fires event `great_holy_war.0004`.

label: Pregnancy ended early
summary: Fires for the mother when a pregnancy ends prematurely.
details: Saved scopes: `scope:mother`, `scope:father` (the assumed father) and `scope:real_father` (the biological father). Vanilla removes the Sacred Childbirth pregnancy health modifier from the mother.

label: Pregnancy revealed (father)
summary: Fires for the father when a pregnancy reaches the revealed status.
details: Saved scopes: `scope:mother`, `scope:father` (the assumed father) and `scope:real_father` (the biological father). The father here is the assumed one. Vanilla's definition has empty event lists.

label: Pregnancy revealed (mother)
summary: Fires for the mother when a pregnancy reaches the revealed status.
details: The root is the mother. Saved scopes: `scope:mother`, `scope:father` (the assumed father) and `scope:real_father` (the biological father). Vanilla lists pregnancy events (a hidden maintenance event, and birth events for a husband's, ex-husband's or bastard child, and a same-sex couple). A mother whose rite has the Sacred Childbirth tenet gets a pregnancy health modifier and a toast.

label: Prestige level gained
summary: Fires when a character gains a prestige level.
details: Vanilla shows a level-gain message. It also raises the `parent_fame_lvl` variable by 1 on each child who remembers the parent becoming very famous.

label: Prestige level lost
summary: Fires when a character loses a prestige level.
details: Vanilla shows a level-loss message. It also changes `parent_fame_lvl` on each child who remembers the parent becoming very famous, but the vanilla script adds 1 here, the same as on level gain, so the variable goes up when the parent loses a level.

label: Primary title changed
summary: Fires when a character's primary title changes.
details: The root is the character; `scope:previous_title` is their old primary title. It does not fire if the new primary title is the same as the old one. Vanilla's definition is empty.

label: Raid action completed
summary: Fires when a raid action finishes.
details: The root is the raid army. Saved scopes: `scope:raider` (the army's owner), `scope:barony` (the raided barony) and `scope:county`. Vanilla fires several raiding events (by their comments: a personal raid on a county capital, prisoners, artifact theft, intent effects), tells the raider, may start a legend seed, damages house relations, and puts a looted modifier on the province for 5 years. Unless the county holder has the Enduring Hardships perk, it also lowers county control, followed by a random draw that can cost development progress. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest is not shown.

label: Raid action started
summary: Fires when a raid action starts.
details: The root is the raid army. Saved scopes: `scope:raider`, `scope:barony` and `scope:county`. Vanilla makes the holder of the barony, and each of their lieges, dislike the raider (the `raided_me_opinion` modifier, with the timer reset if they already had it). It also fires an event where a fearsome target may change the raider's mind, and has a random event that sets up a knight converting to a reformed faith.

label: Raid action weekly
summary: Fires every 7 days while a raid action runs.
details: It does not fire while the raid is stalled by combat. The first call comes 1 to 7 days after the raid starts. The root is the raid army; saved scopes are `scope:raider`, `scope:barony` and `scope:county`. Vanilla's definition is empty.

label: Raid intent invalidated
summary: Fires when a raid intent is invalidated.
details: Vanilla sends the raider (`scope:raider`) a message that the intent is no longer valid. The message names the raiding army, which vanilla passes as the root.

label: Raid loot delivered
summary: Fires when a raider returns to their own territory and deposits loot.
details: The root is the raid army. `scope:raider` is its owner and `scope:raid_loot` the loot gained; `root.raid_loot` shows how much was deposited. Vanilla gives the raider a 3-year flag if they led the army themselves. Its random event list has `chance_to_happen = 25` and a weight-200 empty option beside two setup events of weight 100 each (a child demanding loot, a knight refusing to sacrifice).

label: Rank down
summary: Fires when a title change makes a character drop in the landed tiers, for example from king to duke.
details: The root is the character; `scope:title` is their old primary title. It does not fire during history execution or for dying characters. Vanilla sets a flag `make_suicide_available` for 5 years on most characters (not humble, content or generous) and a variable `rank_demoted`, refreshes embassies for them and their allies, sends the wardens of hostages at their court an event 5 days later, and removes oaths below king tier. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest is not shown.

label: Rank up
summary: Fires when a title change makes a character rise in the landed tiers, for example from duke to king.
details: The root is the character; `scope:title` is their old primary title. It does not fire during history execution or for dying characters. Vanilla keeps the old realm capital for emperors in administrative realms, and shows a coronation reminder to eligible human players. The vanilla text is cut off, so the rest is not shown.

label: Realm capital changed
summary: Fires when a realm capital changes.
details: This happens on a manual move, loss in conquest, a move after inheritance, a grant of a better title, or becoming landed for the first time. The root is the new capital barony; `scope:holder` is the character changing capital (the same character can change several times at once, so check the holders match) and `scope:old_capital` the previous barony, which can be empty or owned by someone else. Vanilla re-applies a vizier's extravagance modifiers so their text no longer names a place they lost, and for the holder of the papal state title runs an effect that enforces the papal court language. The vanilla text is cut off.

label: Release from prison
summary: Fires when a character is released from prison.
details: The root is the released character and `scope:imprisoner` the one who held them. It does not fire when they leave prison by dying. Vanilla may update the legend chapter of a promoted legend (75 percent chance), creates a release memory unless the character just escaped, removes some prison-related modifiers and flags, and makes the imprisoner a rival if the prisoner was marked for that. The vanilla text is cut off.
